_about: Spoken lines for the recorded demo, written for a calm voice-over of about two minutes a video. Keys are the walkthrough screenshot ids (the video holds on each one as long as its line takes to say; an empty line is a short hold) plus '<part>:signin:<role>' (said while the login is typed; ':2' is a second sign-in of the same role). There are no intro cards. Rule: name the role every time (the student, the Dean, Graduate School staff); never a pronoun for a person. Edit a line, re-run record_demo.py and build_narration.py: the pause follows the length of the line.
monitoring-sheet-01: The Monitoring Sheet, under Records: one row per student, one column per subject. Colours show completed, enrolled, or not yet taken.
monitoring-sheet-02: Graduate School staff adds a student missing from the imported sheet. The window warns: manual entry, recorded with the staff member's name and time.
monitoring-sheet-03: Student ID, name and year of entry. The same required fields and duplicate checks as an import apply.
monitoring-sheet-04: The student is added, with a Student Portal login.
monitoring-sheet-05: The record panel lists all eighteen subjects, none taken yet, with units counted automatically.
monitoring-sheet-06: Graduate School staff adds a subject: status Completed, the term, and a remark.
monitoring-sheet-07: Both rows say Manual entry in the Source column, so manual data is never mistaken for imported data.
monitoring-sheet-08: A remark is corrected with a simple edit.
monitoring-sheet-09: Removing a row needs a reason. The row returns to not taken and stays in the history.
monitoring-sheet-11: The Change history tab shows every add, change and removal: old value, new value, who, when, source and reason. That is the audit trail.
monitoring-sheet-12: Back on the grid, the new student carries a Manual tag, and hand-entered cells show an orange dot.
monitoring-sheet-13: Now an imported student. Every row says Imported: official workbook values.
monitoring-sheet-14: Changing an imported value requires a reason, recorded with the staff member's name. Grades are never entered here: AIMS is the official source.
2h-1:signin:Student: Daniel, a Master of Arts in Education student, signs in.
leave-of-absence-01: Under Requests, Leave of Absence. The form shows the limits: two semesters at a time.
leave-of-absence-02: Rules applied on this screen lists each rule with its Handbook page.
leave-of-absence-03: Daniel picks the dates, a reason, and a short explanation.
leave-of-absence-04: A summary to check before sending.
leave-of-absence-05: Submitted. The request waits for Graduate School staff.
leave-of-absence-06: The Leave of Absence board: stages are columns, requests are cards.
leave-of-absence-07: Graduate School staff drags the card to In staff review. The server checks every move.
leave-of-absence-10: The policy check advises with Pass or Needs review. It never decides. The Dean does.
leave-of-absence-11: Graduate School staff forwards the request to the Dean.
leave-of-absence-12: The card moves to With the Dean and locks for staff.
leave-of-absence-14: The Dean drags the card to Leave scheduled.
leave-of-absence-15: Approved, flagged for the Registrar. The Dean could also deny it.
leave-of-absence-17: For the demo, Graduate School staff starts the leave by hand.
leave-of-absence-18: Daniel is on leave, and enrollment is closed.
leave-of-absence-19: The Registrar list. The portal sends no e-mail: staff sends it officially.
leave-of-absence-21: Graduate School staff marks the list sent to the Registrar.
leave-of-absence-22: The student's page shows the status On leave.
2h-2:signin:Student: Therese, a student on approved leave, signs in to come back.
readmission-01: The Readmission page: enrollment stays closed until readmission is approved. The leave being ended is pre-filled.
readmission-02: The rule: a returning student writes an intent to enroll, Handbook page fifty-three.
readmission-03: Therese picks the return semester, gives a reason, and confirms the four checklist items.
readmission-05: Submitted, to Graduate School staff and then the Dean.
readmission-06: The Readmission board has the same layout with its own columns. Therese's card is in Submitted.
readmission-08: The request shows the return semester, the intention, and the linked leave.
readmission-09: The checklist shows what the student ticked, not yet verified, and the leave history.
readmission-10: The policy check flags an early return. Only the Dean can allow that, so it shows Needs review.
readmission-11: Forwarding, Graduate School staff ticks the items verified. Anything unticked reaches the Dean as Needs review.
2h-2:signin:Dean: The Dean signs in to decide.
readmission-14: The Dean approves the return, with a note.
readmission-15: Therese is active again. Readmission restores standing but does not enroll subjects. The Academic Coordinator does that next.
readmission-16: The staff board now shows the Academic Coordinator as next owner, flagged for the Registrar.
readmission-17: The same Registrar list: download, send, mark sent, then acknowledged.
readmission-18: Therese sees the approval, with messages from staff and the Dean.
awol-01: The AWOL and Residency board flags cases from imported enrollment records. Nobody types AWOL.
awol-02: Maya Torres's card sits in AWOL, Waiting for: Student. Staff cannot move it; only the student can start a return.
awol-03: Residence limits apply: master's, five years normal and seven absolute; doctorate, seven and nine. Leave time counts.
awol-04: The card shows the AWOL date, the flag's source and the last enrolled semester.
awol-05: The Return from AWOL page shows the flag. Registration stays restricted until review.
awol-06: Maya picks the return semester and last enrolled semester, and writes the reason.
awol-08: Submitted. The system checks that Maya is within the maximum residence.
awol-09: On the staff board, the card moves itself to Return review.
awol-10: The request shows the intention and the residence limits.
awol-11: Graduate School staff forwards it to the Dean with a note.
awol-14: The Dean drags the card to Back in the program. Approval restores standing.
awol-16: The Academic Coordinator is next owner, since enrollment is a separate step.
awol-18: The Registrar list holds one report per approved return, downloaded and sent officially.
awol-19: Maya sees the approval. Leave, return and AWOL all run on the same board, request window and Registrar list.
reports-tour-01: Reports and Analytics, under Overview. Filters on top: program, entry cohort and period. Below, the six numbers the office asks about most.
reports-tour-02: Behind schedule: the share of active students who are behind, against a target.
reports-tour-03: Median days to decide, against the twelve months before. Every number is computed from recorded events.
reports-tour-04: Needs attention. Each bar is a cause; the longest affects the most students.
reports-tour-05: Selecting a cause narrows the list to the students affected.
reports-tour-06: Show all causes restores the list, most delayed first, with the office that can move each student on. Download it as Excel or PDF.
reports-tour-07: Where students get stuck counts students per stage as on time, slow or stuck.
reports-tour-07b: Every count is a button that opens the real students behind it.
reports-tour-08: Office speed: which offices take longest to close requests. The longest red bar marks the office to ask first.
reports-tour-09: Records to fix lists research students with missing records, such as no adviser. A fixed record drops off.
reports-tour-11: Graduation candidates: who can graduate and what is missing.
reports-tour-12: Overdue and pending: each waiting task, longest first.
reports-tour-13: Defenses held and upcoming, with panel and verdict.
reports-tour-14: Registrar changes: the daily list the Registrar must apply in AIMS.
reports-tour-15: Every filter covers the whole page. One program picked, and all the numbers follow.
best-features-01: First, rules with a source. Every rule the workflows follow sits in one register, with its Handbook or Protocol page and a label: enforced, only documented, or needs review.
best-features-02: Searching a topic lists the matching rules, each with its page.
best-features-03: Second, the Policy Assistant answers only from the Graduate School's own documents. Ask one question, and the answer names its source.
best-features-04: This site runs without the Gemini key, so this is the offline answer. The source opens to the exact passage.
best-features-05: Third, panel matching that explains itself. Each faculty member gets a score out of one hundred.
best-features-06: The breakdown is on screen: expertise, availability and workload, with the passage that matched. A person still chooses the panel.
best-features-07: Fourth, scheduling that checks before booking. It reads availability and suggests the best shared times.
best-features-08: Hard stops, such as a double-booked panelist or room, cannot be overridden. Warnings, such as the lead time, need a recorded reason.
best-features-09: Fifth, shared boards. Leave, readmission, AWOL, withdrawal, practicum and graduation run on the same staged boards, and every move is recorded.
best-features-10: Reports and Analytics are computed from those records, not typed in.
best-features-11: Each feature takes data the Graduate School already has, plus the governing policy, and turns it into a decision, a warning or a measurement.
best-features-12: The honest limits: the portal sends no e-mail, Google Calendar is optional, official data comes only from AIMS, and rules marked Needs review wait for validation. Thank you.
